question: The star S2 circles the Milky Way's central black hole every 16 years, about 1,000 Earth–Sun distances out. How many million suns is the hole?
move: Anything in orbit weighs what it circles; time the orbit, not the object.
trap: Forgetting to square the period, which gives 62 million.
hint: In Earth–Sun distances and years, an orbit's size cubed over its period squared gives the mass in suns.
steps: Kepler, in these units: mass in suns = distance cubed / period squared.
reference: GRAVITY Collaboration, Detection of the Schwarzschild precession in the orbit of the star S2 near the Galactic centre massive black hole, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 2020
